# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)
- Victim example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

## Constraints

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.
- No schema changes required.
- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`. If false, the audit is treated as stale.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — Audit command integration point
- `src/pi-audit.ts` — Pi audit module

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO** — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations (complementary; prevents timestamp churn, this handles post-invalidation review)
- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child of WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Established the audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Inspecting changes since audit could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Only run when freshness check fails; use efficient diff comparison.
- **Backward compatibility:** Existing audit behavior must be preserved for items with no previous audit result.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What specific change types should the audit skill inspect when deciding whether to re-instate an audit? — A: Anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it. So description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages etc. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: Should this be automatic (triggered when an invalidated audit is discovered) or manual (operator/producer-initiated)? — A: Automatic. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: How does this relate to WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)? — A: Complementary — WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO prevents timestamp churn from invalidating audits, this item handles post-invalidation review to determine whether to re-instate or re-run. Source: interactive reply (producer).

# Dispatcher workspace has a useless blank pane

## Problem statement

When the Dispatcher workspace is created via `herdr workspace create --label Dispatcher --no-focus`, herdr automatically provisions a root pane. This root pane is persisted as the legacy `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` but is never adopted by any tab — the Dispatcher workspace sits with a blank, unused pane alongside the per-prefix tabs that carry the actual downtime dispatch work.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher operator** (Map/agent): the Dispatcher workspace should display only productive tabs, not a blank pane that adds clutter.
- **herdr interactive user**: a neutral workspace should show relevant panes only.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No blank root pane on first provision**: when the Dispatcher workspace is provisioned for the first time, the workspace's initial root pane must be adopted (as a tab or otherwise) rather than left blank — the workspace should contain only panes that serve the dispatch purpose.
2. **Idempotent re-provisioning**: on subsequent dispatch cycles, the existing workspace is reused without creating additional blank panes; if the root pane is closed, it is not replaced by a new blank pane.
3. **Per-prefix tab anchors preserved**: the existing tab-anchor mechanism (one tab per work-item prefix, persisted in `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`) continues to function correctly — each prefix still maps to a tab with an alive anchor pane.
4. **No regression to dispatch**: all downtime dispatch flows continue to route to the correct project CWD and pane placement; `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <pane-id>` works with the new layout.
5. **Test coverage**: existing `packages/herdr` test suite passes; new/updated tests cover the provision path.

## Constraints

- The fix must be within `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` and related files — do not modify `send-to-pi.sh` or `grid.py`.
- Must respect `--no-focus` semantics (never steal focus from the user's interactive workspace).
- Must be concurrency-safe (coordination lock pattern already established).
- Must not break the backward-compatible anchor file format (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` → `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`).

## Existing state

- `getDispatcherAnchor()` creates the workspace and stores the root pane ID in `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`.
- `getDispatcherTabAnchor()` creates per-prefix tabs inside the workspace, each with its own root pane.
- The workspace root pane (the anchor) is never adopted by any tab — it sits blank.
- Code: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor()` lines ~451–504, `createWorkspace` in deps ~98–113.

## Desired change

Provision the Dispatcher workspace such that the initial root pane is adopted as the first tab's pane (e.g. a generic "Downtime" tab or the first prefix tab). The root pane must remain alive to preserve the anchor file semantics.

**Validation against herdr 0.9.0 CLI:**
- `herdr workspace create` has no option to suppress the root pane — it is always created.
- `herdr pane move <pane-id> --tab <tab-id> --no-focus` can move a pane into an existing tab.
- `herdr pane move <pane-id> --new-tab --tab-label <label> --no-focus` can move a pane into a new tab.
- `herdr pane close` exists but must NOT be used for the anchor pane — closing it would break the `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <pane-id>` dispatch path, and `getDispatcherAnchor`'s stale detection would re-provision a new blank pane (infinite blank-pane loop).

**Recommended approach:**
1. After `deps.createWorkspace(DISPATCHER_WORKSPACE_LABEL)` returns `{ workspaceId, paneId }`, the root pane is at `paneId`.
2. Create a tab: `herdr tab create --workspace <ws-id> --label Downtime --no-focus`.
3. Move the root pane into the tab: `herdr pane move <rootPaneId> --tab <tabId> --no-focus`.
4. Close the tab's own root pane (created by `tab create`): `herdr pane close <tabRootPaneId>`.
5. Persist the anchor with the moved pane ID — it is now a tab pane.

**Constraints applied:** `--no-focus` on all CLI calls. Coordination lock pattern reused for concurrency safety.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — `getDispatcherAnchor()`, `createWorkspace()` in deps
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatch path, uses `getDispatcherAnchor` / `getDispatcherTabAnchor`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wiring of dispatcher anchor resolver
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — unit tests for anchor provisioning

## Related work

- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG** (completed): Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace) — parent of the anchor provisioning work.
- **WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U** (completed): Implement dispatcher anchor provisioning (Anchor module) — child of C0, implemented the anchor.
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC** (open): Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) — child of C0, implemented per-prefix tabs.

## Headline

The Dispatcher workspace created by `herdr workspace create --label Dispatcher --no-focus` carries a blank root pane that is persisted but never adopted by any tab — it sits unused alongside the per-prefix dispatch tabs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `herdr workspace create` always creates a root pane. **Confirmed** — no CLI option to suppress.
- **Assumption**: The root pane can be adopted by a tab. **Confirmed** — `herdr pane move --tab` and `--new-tab --tab-label` provide the mechanism.
- **Assumption**: No code path depends on the workspace having a live root pane. **Confirmed** — consumers use the pane returned by `getDispatcherAnchor` / `getDispatcherTabAnchor` as the anchor target, not the workspace root.
- **Risk**: Closing the root pane would break dispatch and trigger a re-provision loop (stale detection → new blank pane). Avoided by adopting the pane into a tab instead.
- **Scope**: Minimal — only touch `getDispatcherAnchor` provision path. Per-prefix tab anchors (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC) are unaffected.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'reused' mean — adopt the root pane as a tab, close it, or something else?" — Answer (code analysis): The root pane created by `herdr workspace create` is never adopted by any tab; tabs created via `herdr tab create` get their own root panes. Proposed fix: close the root pane after workspace creation, or adopt it as the first tab's pane. Source: code analysis of `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`.
- Q: "Can the root pane be closed via herdr CLI?" — Answer: `herdr pane close <pane-id>` exists and should work. Needs validation in implementation. Source: herdr CLI help.
- Q: "Should the per-prefix tab system be modified to adopt the root pane instead of closing it?" — Answer (preferred): If feasible, the root pane should be adopted as the first tab's pane. If not, closing it is the fallback. Source: code analysis — tabs always create new panes.
- Q: "What about the legacy `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` format?" — Answer: It should be deprecated in favour of the tab anchor format (`downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`). Source: existing code already uses both files.
- Q: "Can the root pane be moved into a tab via herdr CLI?" — Answer (validated): **Yes.** `herdr pane move <pane-id> --tab <tab-id> --no-focus` and `--new-tab --tab-label <label>` are available in herdr 0.9.0. **Preferred approach confirmed.** Source: `herdr pane move --help`, CLI verification.

Closing it breaks dispatch and triggers `getDispatcherAnchor`'s stale-detection re-provision loop, creating a new blank pane. **Closing the anchor pane is not a viable approach.** Source: code analysis of `getDispatcherAnchor` stale-detection logic and `downtime-worker.ts` dispatch path.

# Downtime dispatcher should dispatch into project workspace (WL-0MU321YK70035AYT)

**Headline**: Change the herdr downtime dispatcher so that an automated pane for a work item written in project `R` spawns inside the herdr workspace that hosts the herdr plugin (worklist) pane for `R`, instead of the machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace and its per-prefix tabs.

## Problem statement

Automated downtime dispatches currently spawn into a dedicated machine-wide `Dispatcher` workspace — anchored by a persisted anchor pane (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`) and, after C1, routed by work-item prefix into per-prefix tabs inside that workspace (`downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`). The producer rejected per-project tabs ("We are not getting per project tabs", audit on WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC). The desired behaviour is that dispatched panes land in the project's own herdr workspace — specifically the workspace/tab that contains the herdr plugin pane for that project — so automated work is co-located with the project it belongs to and the operator sees it where they are already working.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running 2+ project workspaces** (e.g. ContextHub `WL`, Tableau Card Engine `CG`, AI Hell `AH`, SorraAgents `SA`):
  > "As an operator, I want automated downtime panes for project `X` to appear in project `X`'s herdr workspace (next to that project's Worklog plugin pane), so I do not have to visit a separate neutral workspace or hunt for the right tab."
- **Overnight / on-call dispatch reviewer**:
  > "As an on-call engineer, I want each project's automated panes to sit with that project's workspace, so a project's overnight activity is visible in context and never intermixed with another project's."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Project-workspace placement** — for an automated dispatch of work item `<PREFIX>-<hash>` whose worklog root is `R`, the spawned `Downtime triggered …` pane's `workspace_id` equals the herdr workspace that hosts the herdr plugin/worklist pane (`label == "Work Items"`) whose logical project root is `R`; verified with `herdr pane list` (new pane's `workspace_id`) and `herdr tab list` (the plugin pane's workspace/tab). No dispatched pane for root `R` lands in the `Dispatcher` workspace or in another project's workspace.
2. **Deterministic project→workspace resolution** — resolution matches the candidate's `worklogRoot` against the plugin pane's logical project root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, readable via `herdr pane process-info --pane <id>` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`), not against pane `cwd` (which for plugin panes is the plugin directory) and not against the workspace label. Resolution is fail-closed on ambiguity/failure, and never falls back to the leader's pane or another project's workspace. (Exact fallback policy when no plugin pane exists is an OPEN QUESTION — see Appendix Q2.)
3. **Placement within the project workspace** — the anchor used to split is the project's plugin pane (so the new pane appears in the same tab as the worklist), per the duplicate item WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0. (Alternative placements are an OPEN QUESTION — see Appendix Q3.)
4. **Rejected C0/C1 machinery retired from the worklog dispatch path** — per-prefix tab routing (`getDispatcherTabAnchor`, `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`) is removed from the worklog dispatch path (code, tests, docs and persisted-file readers retired); the `Dispatcher` anchor is no longer used for worklog-item dispatch. (Whether the `Dispatcher` workspace and its anchor file are removed entirely or retained for any no-project case is an OPEN QUESTION — see Appendix Q2.)
5. **No regression to dispatch correctness** — selection/ranking (Herdr list head), coordination, round-robin, CAS claim (`--if-status/--if-stage`), staged-marker exclusion, `code-freeze` and `needsProducerReview` gates, per-item `cwd` forwarding, pane naming, and the dispatch audit log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, `downtime-log.ts` kinds) remain unchanged.
6. **Applied to every automated downtime spawn** — worklog tiers and scheduled prompts (which carry a worklog root `cwd`) use the same project-workspace resolution; manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows are unchanged.
7. **Tests** — unit/integration coverage for: resolution success (root → plugin workspace/tab), no-plugin-pane handling, multiple-plugin-pane handling, malformed `herdr pane list`/`process-info` output (fail-closed), anchor forwarding to `send-to-pi.sh --anchor`, and removal of per-prefix tab routing from the worklog path; all existing `packages/herdr` tests adjusted and green.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Automated downtime dispatch only (`dispatchClaimedTier` / `dispatchFromCoordination` / `dispatchScheduledPrompt`); manual `open-worklist` / `open-pi-agent` flows keep current behaviour.
- Reuse the existing spawn surface: `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` (`pane split --pane`) and `grid.py`; do not invent a new pane-creation mechanism.
- Reuse existing fail-closed conventions (no pane, no marker on an unresolvable target) — an unresolved project workspace must never silently fall back to the wrong project.
- Any provisioning/coordination must use the existing machine coordination dir (`~/.herdr/downtime`, `machine-coordination.ts`) and lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock`) — no new lock mechanism.
- herdr CLI output shape varies (`pane_id`/`paneId`, nested `result`) — parsers tolerate variants and log raw output on parse failure (existing convention).

## Existing state

- **C0 (WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG, completed)** added `dispatcher-anchor.ts`: `getDispatcherAnchor()` provisions one `Dispatcher` workspace + anchor pane, persisted to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`, and `dispatchClaimedTier` forwards its pane id as `anchorId`.
- **C1 (WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC, open, audit rejected "We are not getting per project tabs.")** added `getDispatcherTabAnchor()`: routes `<PREFIX>` (`candidate.id.split('-', 1)[0]`) to a tab labelled with the prefix inside the `Dispatcher` workspace, persisted to `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json`. Live state today: `Dispatcher` workspace `w34` holds prefix tabs `WL`, `AH`, `SA`, `CG`, `OSL`; the live anchor file points at `w36:p1`.
- **Live evidence for the target mapping** (this host): each project workspace hosts a plugin pane with `label == "Work Items"`; `herdr pane process-info --pane w2V:pB` → `shell_pid` whose `/proc/<pid>/environ` carries `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` and `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w2V`. Similarly `w2Y:pW` → `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w2Y`. The plugin pane's reported `cwd` is the plugin directory (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`), so resolution must use `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, not `cwd`.
- **Scheduled prompts** (`dispatchScheduledPrompt`) carry `opts.cwd` = the project's worklog root and currently resolve the `Dispatcher` anchor; they can use the same project-workspace resolver.
- **Duplicate/related item**: `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` "Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace" (open, `idea`, high) states the same intent — "spawned in the same tab as the herdr extension for that project". See OPEN QUESTION Q1.

## Desired change

1. Add a project-workspace resolver (in `dispatcher-anchor.ts` or a sibling module) that, given a worklog root `R`, returns the anchor pane of the herdr plugin pane for `R` (`{ paneId, workspaceId, tabId } | null`), by enumerating `herdr pane list`, filtering plugin panes (`label == "Work Items"`), reading each plugin pane's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` via `herdr pane process-info` + `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`, and matching `R`.
2. Wire it into `dispatchClaimedTier` (replacing `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor` for the worklog path) and into `dispatchScheduledPrompt`; forward the resolved pane id as `anchorId` so `send-to-pi.sh --anchor <paneId>` splits the project plugin pane and `grid.py` rebalances in that workspace/tab.
3. Retire the C1 per-prefix tab machinery from the worklog dispatch path and stop writing/reading `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` for worklog dispatch.
4. Add tests and update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` accordingly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — new project-workspace/plugin-pane resolver (`herdr pane list` + `pane process-info` + `/proc` env read); retire per-prefix tab provisioning/persistence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` anchor resolution (replace per-prefix path); `dispatchScheduledPrompt` anchor resolution; dep type changes.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` / `defaultDispatcherAnchorResolver` / `defaultDispatcherTabAnchorResolver` wiring; new resolver dep.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — resolution + integration tests; remove/adjust per-prefix tab tests.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` / `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — no behavioural change expected (anchor is any pane id); verify.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` / `downtime-dispatch-tab-anchors.json` — persisted files (retire the tab-anchors file; fate of the anchor file per Q2).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — replace the C0/C1 placement sections with the project-workspace invariant.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: no plugin pane open for a project** → the dispatcher cannot resolve a target. Fail-closed (no dispatch) is the safe default but can starve a project; fallback policy is Q2.
- **Risk: multiple plugin panes for one root** (operator opened several `Worklog` tabs across workspaces) → ambiguous target. Assumption: choose deterministically (e.g. the focused/first matching pane by pane id); confirm during implementation.
- **Risk: `/proc` env read is Linux-specific and requires the shell_pid from `pane process-info`.** This is the same mechanism already used by `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`; acceptable on this host (Linux). Non-Linux degradation → fail-closed.
- **Risk: splitting the plugin pane shrinks the worklist** and may disturb the operator's layout. `grid.py` rebalance mitigates; alternative placements are Q3.
- **Risk: scope creep** — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane" (WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU) and leftover `Dispatcher` workspaces are adjacent cleanup; keep them out of scope unless Q2 chooses removal.
- **Assumption:** plugin panes are identifiable by `label == "Work Items"` (the plugin pane entrypoint title) and carry `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` + `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` in the shell process environment.
- **Assumption:** scheduled prompts use the same project-workspace resolution as worklog dispatch (their `cwd` is the project worklog root).
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — changing selection/ranking, the audit freshness gate, or the coordination/leader model; any such follow-ups get their own work items.

## Related work

- **WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0 — "Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace"** (open, `idea`, high) — the same intent ("spawned in the same tab as the herdr extension for that project"). This item must be reconciled before implementation (Appendix Q1).
- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG — "Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace)"** (completed) — the C0 design this item reverses; children `WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U`, `WL-0MTR2HLLJ009PTPJ`, `WL-0MTR2JOTE006T3XT`.
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC — "Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace"** (open, `plan_complete`, audit rejected) — the C1 per-prefix tab work this item retires; rejected by producer with "We are not getting per project tabs."
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX — "Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace"** (completed) — the incident that motivated the Dispatcher anchor; context for why placement was moved out of project workspaces, now being moved back deliberately.
- **WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane"** (open, `intake_complete`) — adjacent cleanup of the `Dispatcher` workspace; likely becomes moot if this item retires that workspace.
- **WL-0MU2LF6SZ000JQYI / WL-0MU2LFHBH004VF48** (completed) — C1 per-prefix anchor provisioning and docs/integration tests that will be retired here.
- **`packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh`** — prior art for reading `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` from a plugin pane's shell process (the resolution mechanism this item needs).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG** – Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace regardless of project (C0: anchor-by-ID into dedicated Dispatcher workspace) (completed)
- **WL-0MLSHA2FE0T8RR8X** – Implement multi-directory plugin discovery with precedence (completed)
- **WL-0MS6LS2TF007AV63** – Implement tab working directory support in herdr plugin (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptable, acceptance, activity, add, added (+286 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mtr01eu7005syzg, 0mtrqt482001snxc, add, added, agent (+279 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mtr01eu7005syzg, activity, add, added, agent (+215 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### OPEN QUESTION Q1 — duplicate item reconciliation

- Q: "`WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` ("Dispatched panes should go under the project workspace", open/`idea`/high) describes the same change — "spawned in the same tab as the herdr extension for that project". Both items cannot be implemented independently. How should we reconcile them? Options: (a) keep `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` as canonical and close `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as a duplicate; (b) keep `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as canonical and close this item as a duplicate; (c) make one a child of the other; (d) implement both separately." — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Party asked: producer/operator. Evidence: identical intent in both descriptions; `/skill:find-related` did not surface the other item, but a direct `wl search "Dispatcher workspace"` did.
  **Recommended:** (a) keep `WL-0MU321YK70035AYT` as canonical and close `WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0` as a duplicate — this item is the one currently dispatched and being intaken, and it is explicitly tied to the C1 rejection.

### OPEN QUESTION Q2 — fallback when no plugin pane exists for the item's project

- Q: "When a dispatch candidate belongs to worklog root `R` but no live herdr plugin pane for `R` can be resolved, what should the dispatcher do? Options: (a) fail-closed — no dispatch this cycle (never a wrong-project fallback), leaving the item for a later cycle when the project is open; (b) fall back to the existing `Dispatcher` workspace anchor (retain `downtime-dispatch-anchor.json` and its provisioning for this case only); (c) fall back to the leader's current pane; (d) skip the candidate and continue to the next candidate." — **Status: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Party asked: producer/operator. Evidence: current code fails closed on `anchor-unavailable`; the 2026-09 31 h zero-dispatch incident (documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) shows fail-closed can starve work if the target is persistently unresolvable.
  **Recommended:** (a) fail-closed (never wrong-project placement), and keep the `Dispatcher` machinery only as an *optional, explicit* fallback if the producer prefers (b) — this also decides whether the `Dispatcher` workspace/anchor file is retired entirely.

# Problem statement

The `a-r` (audit reject) chord in herdr fails with `bash: -c: unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`'` when the user-entered rejection reason contains an apostrophe. The `substituteIdentifiers` function in `form-dialog.ts` performs raw string replacement, inserting user text into a shell command template where the placeholder sits inside single quotes — an unescaped apostrophe terminates the quote early.

## Headline

Fix `a-r` audit reject shortcut to properly shell-escape user-entered reason text, preventing bash parsing errors when the reason contains apostrophes or other shell metacharacters.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators who reject audited work items via `a-r` and need to explain why.
- **Secondary**: Any user running chord commands with user-provided text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `a-r` shortcut handles reason text containing apostrophes, double quotes, dollar signs, backticks, and other shell metacharacters without breaking.
2. The audit-set summary is correctly persisted with the full reason text, verbatim.
3. All other chord commands (a-y approve, producer review, update, search, note-edit, prompt) continue to handle valid input unchanged.
4. Regression tests verify shell metacharacter safety for user-provided shortcut values.
5. All existing herdr tests pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — `substituteIdentifiers` does raw replacement; needs shell-escaping
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `a-r` command template embeds `<reason>` in single quotes
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — form dialog dispatches the substituted command
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `buildRunInPaneArgs` / `run-in-pane.sh` execution path

## Constraints

- Fix must not change the `a-r` chord key binding or its visible behaviour (form dialog, pane, confirmation).
- The fix should be scoped to `substituteIdentifiers` in `form-dialog.ts`; avoid changes to `wl` CLI unless necessary.
- Must work cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk**: Escaping strategy must cover all shell metacharacters (quotes, backticks, `$()`, `|`, `&`, `;`, `\`, newlines). **Mitigation**: use `printf '%q'` or equivalent well-tested escaping; test with comprehensive metacharacter set.
- **Risk**: Other shortcuts with user-provided identifiers (`<producer_comment>`, `<search_term>`, `<status>`, `<stage>`, `<title>`, `<description>`, `<prompt>`, `<note_text>`) likely share the same vulnerability. **Mitigation**: document as a follow-up; scope this item to `a-r` only.
- **Risk**: Changing the escaping strategy may require updating all shortcut templates to remove pre-existing quotes. **Mitigation**: if template changes are needed, apply consistently across all shortcuts in this item.
- **Risk**: Choosing a file-based approach (`--summary-file`) for `wl audit-set` adds complexity. **Mitigation**: prefer shell-escaping of the substituted value as the minimal fix; defer file-based approach to follow-up.
- **Risk**: `printf '%q'` output may differ between bash and zsh. **Mitigation**: test on the two most common shells; use `printf '%q'` which is POSIX-compatible in practice.
- **Assumption**: The `a-r` chord is the only shortcut currently reported as broken by metacharacters in user input.
- **Assumption**: `wl audit-set --summary` correctly accepts arbitrary text when properly quoted by the shell.
- **Scope-creep risk**: Fixing all shortcuts at once would be a larger feature. Record as a linked discovery item rather than expanding scope.

## Related work

- WL-0MP082Y1Q003GCUM — Audit internal shell command construction for proper escaping of user text (Worklog src/ only, not herdr)
- WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 — Prevent shell command substitution in wl audit text updates (added --audit-file, but herdr shortcut path still uses --summary in shell)
- WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF — Add --audit-file to wl audit-set (completed, but --summary-file not added)

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK** – Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed)
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** – Stage-based shortcut condition filters (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5JBV0054CBY** – End-to-end test for detail view shortcut result handling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — relevant to shell command execution and pane handling
- `CLI.md` — documents shortcut chords and `a-r` command
- `CHANGELOG.md` — tracks shortcut chord history

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What error occurs when reason text contains an apostrophe?" — Answer (user): `bash: -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`'`. The shell command fails to parse because the apostrophe in the reason text terminates the single-quoted string early. Source: user report. Final: confirmed.
- Q: "Is this the only shortcut affected by this class of bug?" — Answer: Not known yet; other shortcuts with user-provided identifiers (`<producer_comment>`, `<search_term>`, `<title>`, etc.) may have the same vulnerability but have not been reported. Source: code review. Final: likely, but scope this item to `a-r` only.
- Q: "Should we add a --summary-file to wl audit-set instead of shell-escaping?" — Answer: Shell-escaping is the minimal fix; file-based handoff adds complexity and is deferred to follow-up. Source: prior work WL-0MOZUVGL6008QV45 established file-based handoff as the preferred long-term pattern; this item is scoped to the quickest path to fixing the reported bug. Final: shell-escaping for this item.

# Wire `wl interview` into the `r-i` shortcut chord

## Problem statement

The `r-i` chord is documented as "walk through outstanding interview questions on the selected work item", and `shortcuts.json` already maps it to `!!wl interview <id>`. However, the command family is **not recognised by the worklist dispatcher** (`dispatchChordCommand`): it falls through to the generic callback rather than the explicit `!!wl` routes used by `reviewed`/`close`/`delete`/`update`/`search`, it is not treated as a data-modifying command (so the list does not refresh after answers are recorded), and no dispatch-path test covers it. This item is also largely superseded by the completed **WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM**, which added the `r-i` entry.

## Users

- **Map** (agent operator): wants to press `r i` on an item that needs producer review and answer the outstanding clarifying questions in an interactive pane, without leaving the worklist.
  - User story: *As an agent operator, I press `r i` on an item in `in_review` so that `wl interview <id>` opens and I can answer the outstanding questions; when I finish, the list reflects that the item no longer needs producer review.*

## Acceptance Criteria (recommended scope — pending producer confirmation, see Open Questions)

1. The `r-i` chord resolves to `!!wl interview <id>` and the dispatcher recognises the `!!wl interview` family explicitly (it no longer relies solely on the generic fallback); pressing `r i` on a selected item routes `wl interview <id>` into a visible pane.
2. The interview command is treated as a data-modifying command for list-refresh purposes (alongside `close`/`delete`/`update`/`reviewed`/`search`) so the selection list reflects recorded answers / a cleared `needsProducerReview` flag after it completes.
3. At least one automated test asserts the dispatch path: the `r-i` entry resolves to the expected command **and** `dispatchChordCommand` recognises/routes `!!wl interview <id>` (including the resolved id), with `isWlModifyingCommand` covering `interview`. *(testing/validation criterion)*
4. The end-to-end behaviour inside a herdr pane is verified (interview prompts accept input) **or** the non-TTY limitation is explicitly documented if the pane cannot supply interactive stdin. *(validation criterion)*
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The canonical CLI form is `wl interview <id>` (see `CLI.md` §`interview`); `wl <id> interview` is **not** valid CLI syntax. The item title's ordering should be read as referring to the same command.
- The `r` key is already a prefix key (`r-p` Producer Review, `r-i` interview); do not reintroduce a single-key `r` binding.
- If the outcome is "duplicate", the correct action is to close WL-0MU90US3L002HEHF as superseded by WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM — **no code change**.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `r-i` entry present: `"command": "!!wl interview <id>"`, `"label": "interview"` (added by WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM, commit `652ec575`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `dispatchChordCommand` recognises `!!wl reviewed`, `!!wl (close|delete|update|search)`, and compound `&& wl audit-set`; `!!wl interview` is **not** matched. # Unify audit freshness: remove `isAuditNotReadyFresh` competing predicate

## Problem statement

The codebase defines audit freshness **twice**, with different semantics, so the
icon/dispatch paths and the ordering tier can disagree about whether the same
audit is fresh. `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` uses a one-sided time gate
(`auditedAt > updatedAt - AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`, 60 000 ms),
while `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `isAuditNotReadyFresh()` uses a strict
`auditedAt >= updatedAt` with no tolerance. WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE unified only the
icon and dispatch paths; the ordering path was left behind with a competing
predicate. Removing the competitor restores the single-source-of-truth guarantee
and makes all three consumers agree for every input.

## Users and user stories

- **Operator triaging the work queue** — As an operator, when I see the fresh
  audit icon on a work item, the ordering tier should treat that same item as
  audited-not-ready so it is boosted consistently; I should not see an item that
  is "fresh" in one view and "stale" in another.
- **Downtime dispatcher / agent** — As the audit-dispatch path, I rely on the
  single `isAuditFresh` predicate for re-dispatch decisions; no ordering tier
  should be able to contradict it.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want exactly one place that decides audit
  timestamp freshness so future changes cannot silently diverge again.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Single freshness comparison.** `isAuditNotReadyFresh` in
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` is removed, or delegates its timestamp
   comparison to the shared `isAuditFresh`
   (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`), retaining only its `readyToClose === false`
   and audit-presence gates. Verified by a repo search showing the only
   `auditedAt`-vs-`updatedAt` comparison is the shared helper (plus tests that
   intentionally assert it).
2. **Symmetric at-or-near semantics.** The freshness time gate treats an audit
   as fresh when `|auditedAt - updatedAt| < AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`
   (60 000 ms), replacing the current one-sided
   `auditedAt > updatedAt - tolerance`. Verification: unit tests cover inputs on
   both sides of the tolerance boundary.
3. **No re-implementation elsewhere.** No other file re-implements an
   `auditedAt` vs `updatedAt` comparison. Verification: repo search for
   `auditedAt`/`updatedAt` timestamp comparisons returns only the shared helper
   and its consuming call sites.
4. **Consumers agree.** Tests assert that the icon path
   (`auditIcon`/`stageDisplayIcon`), the downtime-dispatch path
   (`selectAuditCandidate`/`hasFreshAudit`), and the ordering path
   (`sortItemsByScore`/`computeScore`/`selectBySortIndex`) return the same
   freshness verdict for: fresh, stale, just-persisted (within tolerance), and
   missing-audit inputs.
5. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
6. **Full suite green.** The full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

7. **Critical tier preserved.** Tests assert a critical item is never outranked by the audit-not-ready boost, and the ordering tier still requires an audit to be present with `readyToClose === false`. Verification: an ordering test places a critical item against a fresh audited-not-ready non-critical item and asserts the critical item ranks first.

## Constraints

- **Fingerprint gate unchanged.** The primary content-fingerprint gate in
  `isAuditFresh` (stored fingerprint == current fingerprint ⇒ fresh) is the
  canonical behaviour and must not be altered; only the fallback time gate is
  affected by the symmetric-semantics change.
- **Preserve the ordering tier's extra gates.** The ordering path also requires
  the audit to exist and `readyToClose === false`; these must be preserved when
  delegating the timestamp comparison.
- **Preserve the hard critical tier.** Critical items must never be outranked by
  the audit-not-ready boost (`sortItemsByScore` comparator boundary).
- **Keep the named tolerance.** `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` keeps its
  name and value (60 000 ms) so documentation and external references stay
  valid.
- **No CHANGELOG edits.** `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.
- **Intake is read-only.** No production code is changed during intake.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS = 60000`
  and `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint?, currentFingerprint?)`;
  the fallback time gate is `auditTime > updateTime - tolerance` (one-sided).
  Header comment claims this is the single source of truth (WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — private `isAuditNotReadyFresh(audit, itemUpdatedAt)`
  (≈ line 658) enforces `readyToClose === false` plus
  `new Date(auditedAt).getTime() >= new Date(updatedAt).getTime()` (strict, no
  tolerance). Consumed by `sortItemsByScore` (≈ lines 705–706),
  `computeScore` (≈ line 2169) and `compareAuditNotReadyTier` (≈ lines 2304–2305,
  used by `selectBySortIndex`).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` does **not** import `isAuditFresh`; the
  `@worklog/shared/icons` imports in database.ts are unrelated (no freshness).
- Consumers already on the shared predicate: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
  (`hasFreshAudit` / dispatch-time gate), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`,
  `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Existing tests exercising the shared predicate: `tests/database.test.ts`,
  `tests/unit/activity-timestamp.test.ts`, `tests/audit-fingerprint-freshness.test.ts`,
  `tests/integration/audit-skill-cli.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`. `tests/sync.test.ts` and
  `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` contain **inline copies** of the predicate in
  comments/helpers that must be reconciled to the shared helper.

## Desired change

- Make `isAuditFresh`'s fallback time gate symmetric:
  `Math.abs(auditTime - updateTime) < AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`
  (with the existing NaN guard and fail-closed behaviour).
- Remove `isAuditNotReadyFresh`, or reduce it to a thin wrapper that applies the
  `audit` presence + `readyToClose === false` gates and delegates the timestamp
  comparison to `isAuditFresh`, so the ordering tier, the icon path and the
  dispatch path share one definition.
- Update `sortItemsByScore`, `computeScore`, `compareAuditNotReadyTier` (and
  `selectBySortIndex`) to use the delegated predicate.
- Reconcile inline predicate copies in tests to the shared helper.
- Add agreement tests covering fresh / stale / just-persisted / missing-audit
  inputs across the three consumers.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Canonical `isAuditFresh`; change the fallback
  time gate to symmetric at-or-near semantics and update the doc comment.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — Remove `isAuditNotReadyFresh` or delegate
  it to `isAuditFresh`; update the three call sites (`sortItemsByScore`,
  `computeScore`, `compareAuditNotReadyTier`); add the
  `@worklog/shared/icons` import.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatch freshness consumer; verify
  it agrees (likely no change, import already present).
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` — Extend/add symmetric-boundary and
  agreement tests.
- `tests/database.test.ts` — Add ordering-tier agreement tests (fresh / stale /
  just-persisted / missing audit).
- `tests/audit-fingerprint-freshness.test.ts` — Adjust/add time-gate cases if the
  symmetric change affects expected outcomes.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`,
  `tests/unit/activity-timestamp.test.ts` — Reconcile inline predicate copies /
  expectations with the shared helper.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** The tolerance stays 60 000 ms and the fingerprint gate remains
  primary; the symmetric change applies only to the fallback time gate.
- **Risk — canonical semantics mismatch.** AC2 states symmetric
  `|auditedAt - updatedAt| < tolerance`, but the referenced SorraAgents
  implementation (`_audit_time_is_fresh`, SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 /
  SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM) is asymmetric: fresh when
  `audit > update + 60s`, **plus** a reverse persistence window
  `0 <= update - audit <= PERSIST_TOLERANCE`. Mitigation: implement AC2 as
  written but add regression tests for audit-later-than-update inputs; flag the
  discrepancy for the producer if behaviour differs materially from the
  canonical gate.
- **Risk — ordering behaviour change for fingerprinted audits.** Delegating to
  `isAuditFresh` means the fingerprint gate *could* apply to ordering; the
  ordering path has no per-item `currentFingerprint` readily available, so the
  delegation must pass no fingerprints (time gate only). Documented as an
  explicit assumption; no extra query is introduced.
- **Assumption:** The strict `>=` vs one-sided `>` difference is subsumed by the
  tolerance window; no consumer relies on exact-equality-only freshness.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Unifying the Python `audit_runner` freshness gate
  (SorraAgents) is out of scope; record as a linked work item, not this task.

## Related work

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE — *Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic
  across icon display and downtime dispatcher* (completed; unified only icon +
  dispatch, left the ordering path competing).
- related-to: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 — *audit_runner parent flow loops re-triggering
  child audits; child freshness can never be satisfied* (completed; canonical
  persistence-window fix).
- related-to: SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM — *Audit staleness race: post-persist comment
  bumps `updatedAt` past `auditedAt`* (defines the reverse persistence window
  in the canonical Python gate).
- Precedent: WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 / WL-0MTHRW3770014H51 — atomic
  `updatedAt = auditedAt` persistence on `saveAuditResult`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** – Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed)
- **WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV** – Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (completed)
- **WL-0MS5UR9MY004UY69** – Align icon prefix in selection list and remove spaces between icons (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, agree, audit, auditedat, behaviour (+67 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: agree, assert, audit, behaviour, call (+58 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: audit, auditedat, behaviour, boost, call (+53 more)

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context, the item description
and repository search supplied a complete problem definition, acceptance
criteria and target files. The one ambiguity identified (AC2 symmetric vs the
canonical SorraAgents asymmetric gate) is recorded above under **Risks and
assumptions** and is testable as written; it does not block intake.

- Research: inspected `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`isAuditFresh`,
  `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`), `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` + 3 call sites), the icon/dispatch consumers, and the
  canonical SorraAgents gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:1287`
  `_audit_time_is_fresh` and the child-gate persistence tolerance at ≈5490).
